text:
maya: Heads up — CI failing on eval-harness for model-onboard. Runner aborts with promptset checksum mismatch in logs.

sam: can you paste the job link / error?

maya: https://ci.redwood/internal/12345 build 2026-03-18T14:22Z -> root error: "Promptset SHA differs from manifest (expected f3a7, found 1b9d) — aborting to avoid silent drift"

eval-bot: run 12345: eval-runner v0.9.2 -> ERROR: promptset_manifest.sha != s3_object.sha (f3a7 vs 1b9d)

oliver: did anyone push a new promptset without bumping the manifest? I pushed new synthetic fixtures yesterday (branch synth/fix) but I thought the PR included the manifest bump.

keisha: I merged synth/fix but I only updated the generator seed in code; I *thought* the CI step would regenerate and bump manifest but maybe that step failed in my PR. checking now.

sam: quick checks: locally `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD:data/promptsets` and then `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-eval --key promptsets/prod.json | jq .ETag` to compare. we need to align repo manifest vs S3 etag.

maya: repro steps I used: ran eval-runner locally with `--promptset=prod` and it pulled s3 object sha 1b9d; manifest in repo expected f3a7. Runner caches by key, and the CI deploy order looks like push->run tests; if two PRs merged in close succession, manifest might reference an artifact that wasn't uploaded yet.

oliver: CI ordering flaw — deploy pipeline: build -> push artifacts -> run tests. If artifact upload and manifest update happen from separate PRs, race possible. We should gate manifest updates on successful artifact upload.

keisha: propose immediate actions: 1) update eval-runner to verify promptset sha at startup and fail fast, 2) add a CI pre-step to assert `s3_etag == manifest.sha`, 3) add a dashboard panel for promptset provenance so ops can see mismatches.

sam: also add a unit test in eval-harness that loads promptset fixture and asserts checksum equals fixture metadata; that'll catch generator/fixture drift in PRs.

maya: temp fix: reuploaded correct promptset file (sha f3a7) and re-ran job — passed. but that's manual; we need automation.

oliver: longer-term: store artifacts at `promptsets/<sha>.json` and have manifest point to the sha. Runner should fetch by sha not by stable name. That avoids races and name-level overwrites.

keisha: yep. And make the generator upload atomic: write to `promptsets/<sha>.json` then update manifest in a single, gated commit.

sam: add a CI lint script: `python tools/check_promptset_provenance.py --manifest data/promptsets/manifest.json` which exits non-zero on mismatch — block merges.

maya: i'll draft an RFC with proposed changes: runner verification, CI gating/lint, artifact-by-sha migration, changelog for promptset versions, and dashboard widget mock. cc @oliver @keisha @sam. will include migration plan and rollback steps.

oliver: i'll help implement runner changes once RFC is up.

eval-bot: NOTE: we also observed a flaky metric after the seed change — generator seed flips invalidate previous baselines. we should require a changelog entry per promptset version indicating whether rebaselining is required.

keisha: good call — add `requires_rebaseline: true/false` in manifest entries and a short `changelog` string.

maya: checklist I'll include in RFC: checksum gating CI, artifact-by-sha migration, runner sha verify, unit test in harness, changelog + rebaseline flag, dashboard panel, and an ops playbook for manual fixes.

sam: :thumbsup: thanks — this should prevent silent drift.

ci-bot: build 12347 rerun queued by @maya (manual retry requested)

maya: i'll post RFC link once ready.
